BiblicalUsage: The word behal means to terrify, and to hasten, and it appears 10 times across the Bible. In Daniel the word does double duty: kings and seers are terrified by what they see, and the same word describes hurrying — Arioch bringing Daniel in haste, and Nebuchadnezzar rising up in haste.
TheologicalSignificance: I hold that holy fear is the right response to God's power, and that the same God who terrifies the proud hurries to save His own. That is why I keep coming back to it: behal is not a word to rush past.
